title: 2026-11-05_CrossRAT_Investigation_and_Containment_fbc
description: Investigate, contain, and remediate the CrossRAT threat on a compromised host.
outcomes: Usage of systemctl for service management

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: CrossRAT is a newly discovered desktop surveillanceware tool capable of targeting Windows, OSX, and Linux systems. It is designed for remote access and control, allowing attackers to exfiltrate data and maintain persistence on infected systems. Security monitoring has detected unusual network activity on the target host, suggesting potential CrossRAT infection. Your task is to investigate, contain, and remediate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) in the cloud sandbox. Use the username 'analyst' and password 'CyberRangeCZ2023!' to log in. Enter 'start' to begin the exercise.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) in the local sandbox. Use the username 'analyst' and password 'CyberRangeCZ2023!' to log in. Enter 'start' to begin the exercise.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the target host using the provided credentials.
2. List all services to identify the suspicious one.
   - Command: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.
4. Identify the service named `bkd.service` as the suspicious one.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl` to list all services and look for any that seem out of place.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the service descriptions for any that mention unusual or suspicious behavior.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system services.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the target host using the provided credentials.
2. Inspect the suspicious service to find the port it is listening on.
   - Command: `systemctl cat bkd.service`
3. Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service file to identify the port.
4. Identify the port number `2223` as the one used for suspicious communication.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl cat` to view the service configuration file.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service file to find the port number.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified as an argument in the `ExecStart` command.

levels.title: Identify Data Collection Service
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the target host using the provided credentials.
2. List all timers to identify the one responsible for periodic execution.
   - Command: `systemctl list-timers --all`
3. Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions.
4. Identify the timer named `local-inventory.timer` as the suspicious one.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The timer responsible for periodic execution will have a name related to inventory or data collection.
